title.zh: 卷73 奚康生 楊大眼 崔延伯
title.en: Volume 73: Xi Kangsheng, Yang Dayan, Cui Yanbo
title.raw: 卷73 奚康生 楊大眼 崔延伯 Volume 73: Xi Kangsheng, Yang Dayan, Cui Yanbo

sentences.zh: 奚康生 楊大眼 崔延伯

translations.literal: Xi Kangsheng, Yang Dayan, Cui Yanbo
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kangsheng, Yang Dayan, and Cui Yanbo

sentences.zh: 奚康生，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Xi Kangsheng was a man of Henan Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kangsheng was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先代人也，世為部落大人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Dai; for generations they were chieftains of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors came from Dai, and for generations they served as tribal chieftains.

sentences.zh: 祖直，平遠將軍、柔玄鎮將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi was General Who Pacifies the Distance and commander of Rouxuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi served as General Who Pacifies the Distance and commander of the Rouxuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 入為鎮北大將軍，內外三都大官，賜爵長進侯。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Great General Who Guards the North, one of the Three Grand Officers of the Inner and Outer [Court], and was granted the title Marquis of Changjin.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Great General Who Guards the North and appointed one of the Three Grand Officers of the Inner and Outer Court, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changjin.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Governor of You Province; his posthumous name was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death, he was posthumously honored as Governor of You Province with the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 父普憐，不仕而卒。

translations.literal: His father Pulian did not take office and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pulian never entered official service and died without office.

sentences.zh: 太和十一年，蠕蠕頻來寇邊，柔玄鎮都將李兜討擊之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taihe, the Rouran repeatedly came to raid the border; Li Dou, chief commander of Rouxuan Garrison, attacked and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Taihe, the Rouran repeatedly raided the frontier. Li Dou, the chief commander of the Rouxuan Garrison, attacked and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 康生性驍勇，有武藝，弓力十石，矢異常箭，為當時所服。

translations.literal: Kangsheng by nature was fierce and brave, possessed martial skills, drew a bow of ten stone strength, and used arrows unlike ordinary ones; he was admired by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng was naturally fierce and courageous, skilled in the martial arts. His bow strength reached ten stone, and he used arrows unlike any ordinary arrow. Men of the time admired him.

sentences.zh: 從兜為前驅軍主，頻戰陷陳，壯氣有聞，由是為宗子隊主。

translations.literal: He followed Dou as commander of the vanguard, frequently fought breaking into battle formations, and his bold spirit became renowned; on this account he became commander of the imperial clan contingent.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Dou as commander of the vanguard, he repeatedly charged into enemy lines in battle, and his bold reputation spread. For this he was made commander of the imperial clan contingent.

sentences.zh: 從駕征鍾離，駕旋濟淮，五將未渡，蕭鸞遣將率眾據渚，邀斷津路。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial campaign against Zhongli; as the emperor turned back and crossed the Huai, five generals had not yet crossed when Xiao Luan sent a general leading troops to occupy the sandbar and intercept and cut the ford route.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the campaign against Zhongli. When the emperor turned back and crossed the Huai River, five generals had not yet crossed. Xiao Luan sent a general with troops to seize a sandbar and block the crossing.

sentences.zh: 高祖敕曰：「能破中渚賊者，以為直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered: "Whoever can break the bandits at the central sandbar shall be made Direct Attendant General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu issued an edict: "Whoever can defeat the enemy at the central sandbar shall be appointed Direct Attendant General.

sentences.zh: 」康生時為軍主，謂友人曰：「如其克也，得暢名績，脫若不捷，命也在天。

translations.literal: " Kangsheng was then a commander; he told a friend: "If one succeeds, one gains free rein for fame and achievement; if one does not prevail, fate lies with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Kangsheng was then a commander. He said to a friend, "If we succeed, I shall win renown for my achievements; if we fail, it is fate.

sentences.zh: 丈夫今日何為不決！

translations.literal: A true man—why on this day not act decisively!
translations.idiomatic: A man today—why should he not be decisive!

sentences.zh: 」遂便應募，縛筏積柴，因風放火，燒其船艦，依烟直進，飛刀亂斫，投河溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he immediately volunteered, bound rafts and piled firewood, took advantage of the wind to set fire, burned their boats and warships, advanced straight through the smoke, hurled flying knives in chaotic chopping, and those who fell into the river and drowned were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately volunteered, bound rafts and piled firewood, and set them afire with the wind to burn the enemy boats. He advanced straight through the smoke, hurling knives left and right; many of the enemy fell into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 乃假康生直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kangsheng was provisionally appointed Direct Attendant General.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng was then provisionally appointed Direct Attendant General.

sentences.zh: 後以勳除中堅將軍、太子三校、西臺直後。

translations.literal: Later, by merit he was appointed Central Strong General, one of the Three Commandants of the Crown Prince, and Direct Attendant at the Western Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his merits he was appointed Central Strong General, one of the Three Commandants of the Crown Prince, and Direct Attendant at the Western Terrace.

sentences.zh: 吐京胡反，自號辛支王。

translations.literal: The Tujing barbarians rebelled and styled themselves King Xinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Tujing barbarians rebelled, and their leader styled himself King Xinzhi.

sentences.zh: 康生為軍主，從章武王彬討之。

translations.literal: Kangsheng served as commander and followed Prince Zhangwu Bin to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng served as a commander and followed Prince Zhangwu of Wei, Yuan Bin, to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 胡遣精騎一千邀路斷截，康生率五百人拒戰，破之，追至石羊城，斬首三十級。

translations.literal: The barbarians sent one thousand elite cavalry to intercept the road; Kangsheng led five hundred men to resist in battle, defeated them, pursued to Shiyang Fort, and severed thirty heads.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent a thousand elite horsemen to block the road. Kangsheng led five hundred men to resist them, defeated the enemy, pursued them to Shiyang Fort, and took thirty heads.

sentences.zh: 彬甲卒七千，與胡對戰，分為五軍，四軍俱敗，康生軍獨全。

translations.literal: Bin had seven thousand armored soldiers; he fought the barbarians, divided into five armies; four armies were all defeated, and Kangsheng's army alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had seven thousand armored soldiers and engaged the rebels in battle. The force was divided into five armies; four were utterly defeated, but Kangsheng's army alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 遷為統軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 率精騎一千追胡至車突谷，詐為墜馬，胡皆謂死，爭欲取之。

translations.literal: Leading one thousand elite cavalry he pursued the barbarians to Chetu Valley, feigned falling from his horse; the barbarians all thought him dead and competed to take him.
translations.idiomatic: Leading a thousand elite horsemen, he pursued the rebels to Chetu Valley and feigned a fall from his horse. The rebels all believed he was dead and rushed to capture him.

sentences.zh: 康生騰騎奮矛，殺傷數十人，胡遂奔北。

translations.literal: Kangsheng leaped onto his horse and brandished his spear, killing and wounding several tens; the barbarians then fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng vaulted onto his horse and swung his spear, killing and wounding several dozen men. The rebels then fled north.

sentences.zh: 辛支輕騎退走，去康生百餘步，彎弓射之，應弦而死。

translations.literal: Xinzhi, with light cavalry, retreated in flight; when he was more than a hundred paces from Kangsheng, [Kangsheng] bent his bow and shot at him; [Xinzhi] died the moment the string was released.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi fled with his light cavalry. When he was more than a hundred paces from Kangsheng, Kangsheng strung his bow and shot; the arrow struck, and Xinzhi fell dead.

sentences.zh: 因俘其牛羊駝馬以萬數。

translations.literal: Thereupon he captured their cattle, sheep, camels, and horses in numbers reaching ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He took captive their cattle, sheep, camels, and horses by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞置義陽□，招誘邊民。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan established Yiyang [lacuna], recruiting and enticing border peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan established Yiyang (lacuna in source) and began recruiting and enticing the frontier populace.

sentences.zh: 康生復為統軍，從王肅討之，進圍其城。

translations.literal: Kangsheng again served as Army Commander, followed Wang Su to attack them, advanced and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng again served as Army Commander and followed Wang Su to attack them, advancing to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 鸞將張伏護自昇城樓，言辭不遜，肅令康生射之。

translations.literal: Luan's general Zhang Fuhu himself ascended the city tower; his words were insolent; Su ordered Kangsheng to shoot him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan's general Zhang Fuhu climbed the city tower and spoke insolently. Wang Su ordered Kangsheng to shoot him.

sentences.zh: 以強弓大箭望樓射窗，扉開即入，應箭而斃。

translations.literal: With a strong bow and great arrow he shot at the tower window; when the door-panel opened the arrow entered, and [Zhang] fell dead upon being struck.
translations.idiomatic: With a powerful bow and a heavy arrow he shot at the tower window. When the shutter opened, the arrow flew in, and Zhang Fuhu fell dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 彼民見箭，皆云狂弩。

translations.literal: The people there, seeing the arrow, all said it was a mad crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders, seeing the arrow, all cried out that it was the shot of a monstrous crossbow.

sentences.zh: 以殺伏護，賞帛一千匹。

translations.literal: For killing Fuhu, he was rewarded with one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: For killing Zhang Fuhu, he was rewarded with one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又頻戰再退其軍，賞三階，帛五百匹。

translations.literal: Again, in frequent battles he twice repelled their army; he was rewarded with three ranks and five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated battles he twice drove the enemy back and was rewarded with three ranks and five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶卷將裴叔業率眾圍渦陽，欲解義陽之急。

translations.literal: Xiao Baojuan's general Pei Shuye led troops to besiege Woyang, intending to relieve the crisis at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baojuan's general Pei Shuye led troops to besiege Woyang, hoping to relieve the pressure on Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 詔遣高聰等四軍往援之，後遣都督、廣陵侯元衍，並皆敗退。

translations.literal: An edict sent Gao Cong and four armies to go aid them; later the Grand Commander, Marquis of Guangling Yuan Yan was also sent—they were all defeated and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Gao Cong and four armies to their aid, and later Grand Commander Yuan Yan, Marquis of Guangling, was sent as well. All were defeated and driven back.

sentences.zh: 時刺史孟表頻啟告，高祖敕肅遣康生馳往赴援。

translations.literal: At the time the governor Meng Biao repeatedly submitted urgent reports; Emperor Gaozu ordered Su to send Kangsheng at full speed to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Meng Biao sent urgent reports one after another, and Emperor Gaozu ordered Wang Su to dispatch Kangsheng at once to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 一戰大破之，賞二階，帛一千匹。

translations.literal: In one battle he greatly defeated them; he was rewarded with two ranks and one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In a single battle he routed the enemy and was rewarded with two ranks and one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 及壽春來降也，遣康生領羽林一千人，給龍廐馬兩匹，馳赴壽春。

translations.literal: When Shouchun came to surrender, [the court] sent Kangsheng leading one thousand Imperial Guard soldiers, granted two Imperial Stud horses, and he galloped to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun surrendered, the court sent Kangsheng at the head of one thousand Imperial Guard soldiers, granted him two horses from the imperial stud, and had him ride at full speed to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 既入其城，命集城內舊老，宣詔撫賚。

translations.literal: Once he entered the city, he was ordered to assemble the old elders within the city and proclaim the edict, comforting and bestowing gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered the city, he was ordered to gather the old residents within the walls, proclaim the imperial edict, and comfort and reward them.

sentences.zh: 俄而，蕭寶卷將桓和頓軍梁城，陳伯之據峡石，民心駭動，頗有異謀。

translations.literal: Before long, Xiao Baojuan's generals Huan He encamped at Liangcheng and Chen Bozhi held Xiashi; the people's hearts were terrified and disturbed, and there were many secret schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Xiao Baojuan's generals Huan He encamped at Liangcheng and Chen Bozhi held Xiashi. The populace was shaken with fear, and many began to plot treachery.

sentences.zh: 康生乃防禦內外，音信不通。

translations.literal: Kangsheng then defended inside and out; communications were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng then fortified the city inside and out, and all communications were severed.

sentences.zh: 固城一月，援軍乃至。

translations.literal: He held the city for one month, and relief troops only then arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He held the city for a month before relief forces finally arrived.

sentences.zh: 康生出擊桓和、伯之等二軍，並破走之，拔梁城、合肥、洛口三戍。

translations.literal: Kangsheng went out to attack the two armies of Huan He, Bozhi, and the rest; he defeated and drove them all off, and captured the three garrisons of Liangcheng, Hefei, and Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng sallied forth to attack the two armies of Huan He and Chen Bozhi, defeated and routed them both, and captured the garrisons at Liangcheng, Hefei, and Luokou.

sentences.zh: 以功遷征虜將軍，封安武縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to General Who Captures the Barbarians, enfeoffed as Founder Baron of Anwu County, with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to General Who Captures the Barbarians, enfeoffed as Founder Baron of Anwu County, with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 出為南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Governor of Southern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Southern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 後蕭衍郁洲遣軍主徐濟寇邊，康生率將出討，破之，生擒濟。

translations.literal: Later, from Yuzhou, Xiao Yan sent Army Commander Xu Ji to raid the border; Kangsheng led his generals out to attack, defeated them, and captured Ji alive.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiao Yan sent Army Commander Xu Ji from Yuzhou to raid the frontier. Kangsheng led his officers out to attack, defeated them, and captured Xu Ji alive.

sentences.zh: 賞帛千匹。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍聞康生能引強弓，力至十餘石，故特作大弓兩張，送與康生。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Yan heard that Kangsheng could draw a strong bow with strength reaching more than ten stone; therefore he specially made two great bows and sent them to Kangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiao Yan heard that Kangsheng could draw a powerful bow of more than ten stone strength, and so he had two great bows made especially and sent them to him.

sentences.zh: 康生得弓，便會集文武，乃用平射，猶有餘力。

translations.literal: Kangsheng received the bows, immediately gathered civil and military officials, then using level shooting still had surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Kangsheng received the bows, he immediately gathered his civil and military officers and, shooting level with the ground, still had strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 其弓長八尺，把中圍尺二寸，箭粗殆如今之長笛，觀者以為希世絕倫。

translations.literal: The bows were eight chi long; the grip measured one chi two cun in circumference; the arrows were as thick as a present-day long flute; onlookers thought them rare in the world and unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: The bows were eight chi long, the grip one chi and two cun around, and the arrows nearly as thick as a modern transverse flute. Onlookers declared them unmatched in the world.

sentences.zh: 弓即表送，置之武庫。

translations.literal: The bows were immediately memorialized and sent [to the capital], and placed in the arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the bows and sent them to the capital, where they were placed in the arsenal.

sentences.zh: 又蕭衍遣將宋黑率眾寇擾彭城，時康生遭母憂，詔起為別將、持節、假平南將軍，領南青州諸軍擊走之。

translations.literal: Again Xiao Yan sent General Song Hei leading troops to raid and harass Pengcheng; at the time Kangsheng was in mourning for his mother; an edict recalled him to serve as Separate Commander, Bearer of the Staff, Provisionally General Who Pacifies the South, commanding the forces of Southern Qing Province, and he struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Again Xiao Yan sent General Song Hei with troops to raid Pengcheng. Kangsheng was then in mourning for his mother, but an edict recalled him to serve as Separate Commander, Bearer of the Staff, and Provisionally General Who Pacifies the South, commanding the armies of Southern Qing Province, and he drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 後衍復遣都督、臨川王蕭宏，[1]副將張惠紹勒甲十萬規寇徐州，又假宋黑徐州刺史，領眾二萬，水陸俱進，徑圍高塚戍。

translations.literal: Later Yan again sent Grand Commander, Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong, [1] deputy general Zhang Huishao mustering armor of one hundred thousand intending to raid Xuzhou; also provisionally appointed Song Hei Governor of Xuzhou, leading twenty thousand troops, advancing by water and land together, directly besieging the Gaozhong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiao Yan again sent Grand Commander Xiao Hong, Prince of Linchuan, [1] with Deputy General Zhang Huishao at the head of one hundred thousand armored men planning to raid Xuzhou. He also provisionally appointed Song Hei Governor of Xuzhou and had him lead twenty thousand men advancing by land and water together to besiege Gaozhong Garrison directly.

sentences.zh: 詔授康生武衞將軍、持節、假平南將軍，為別將，領羽林三千人，騎、步甲士隨便割配。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Kangsheng Guard General, Bearer of the Staff, Provisionally General Who Pacifies the South, as Separate Commander, leading three thousand Imperial Guard, with cavalry and infantry armored soldiers allocated as needed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Kangsheng Guard General, Bearer of the Staff, and Provisionally General Who Pacifies the South, serving as Separate Commander at the head of three thousand Imperial Guard, with cavalry and infantry armored troops assigned as needed.

sentences.zh: 康生一戰敗之。

translations.literal: Kangsheng in one battle defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng defeated them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 還京，召見宴會，賞帛千匹，賜驊騮御胡馬一匹。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital, was summoned and received at a banquet, rewarded with one thousand bolts of silk, and granted one chestnut steed, an imperial tribute horse.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital, was summoned to an audience and a banquet, rewarded with one thousand bolts of silk, and granted one chestnut steed from the imperial tribute horses.

sentences.zh: 出為平西將軍、華州刺史，頗有聲績。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Hua Province, and achieved considerable reputation and accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Hua Province, where he won considerable renown.

sentences.zh: 轉涇州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Jing Province, retaining his original generalship.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Jing Province while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 以輒用官炭瓦為御史所劾，削除官爵。

translations.literal: For presumptuously using official charcoal and tiles he was impeached by the censor, and his office and nobility were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached by the censor for misusing official charcoal and roof tiles, and his office and title were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 尋旨復之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, by imperial favor he was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, by imperial decree he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍直閤將軍徐玄明戍於郁洲，殺其刺史張稷，以城內附。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Direct Attendant General Xu Xuanming garrisoned at Yuzhou, killed its governor Zhang Ji, and brought the city over to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Direct Attendant General Xu Xuanming was garrisoned at Yuzhou. He killed the governor Zhang Ji and offered the city in surrender.

sentences.zh: 詔遣康生迎接，賜細御銀纏槊一張并棗柰果。

translations.literal: An edict sent Kangsheng to welcome him, and granted one fine imperial silver-wrapped spear and jujubes and nashi fruit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Kangsheng to welcome him and granted him one fine imperial silver-wrapped spear, together with jujubes and nashi pears.

sentences.zh: 面敕曰：「果者，果如朕心；

translations.literal: In person the emperor commanded: "As for the fruit—may it indeed accord with my heart;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commanded him in person: "As for the fruit—may it indeed match my heart;

sentences.zh: 棗者，早遂朕意。

translations.literal: as for the jujubes—may they soon fulfill my intent.
translations.idiomatic: as for the jujubes—may they soon fulfill my wish.

sentences.zh: 」未發之間，郁洲復叛。

translations.literal: " Before he had set out, Yuzhou rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could set out, Yuzhou rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 時揚州別駕裴絢謀反，除康生平東將軍，為別將，領羽林四千討之，會事平不行。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Province Assistant Governor Pei Xuan plotted rebellion; Kangsheng was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, as Separate Commander, leading four thousand Imperial Guard to suppress him—but as events settled, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pei Xuan, Assistant Governor of Yang Province, plotted rebellion. Kangsheng was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Separate Commander at the head of four thousand Imperial Guard to suppress him, but the affair was settled before he marched.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，起為平西將軍、西中郎將。

translations.literal: He was in mourning for his father; he was recalled to serve as General Who Pacifies the West and West Central Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for his father, he was recalled from retirement to serve as General Who Pacifies the West and West Central Guard General.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大舉征蜀，假康生安西將軍，領步騎三萬邪趣緜竹。

translations.literal: That year a great campaign was launched against Shu; Kangsheng was provisionally appointed General Who Pacifies the West, leading thirty thousand infantry and cavalry on a diagonal route toward Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: That year a major campaign was launched against Shu. Kangsheng was provisionally appointed General Who Pacifies the West and led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry on an oblique march toward Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 至隴右，世宗崩，班師。

translations.literal: When they reached Longyou, Emperor Xiaoming died, and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Longyou, Emperor Xiaoming died, and the army turned back.

sentences.zh: 除衞尉卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 出為撫軍將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 在州，以天旱令人鞭石虎畫像；

translations.literal: While in the province, because of drought he had people whip the painted image of the stone tiger;
translations.idiomatic: While governing the province, during a drought he had people whip the painted image of the stone tiger;

sentences.zh: 復就西門豹祠祈雨，不獲，令吏取豹舌。

translations.literal: he also went to the shrine of Ximen Bao to pray for rain, and when he did not obtain it, he ordered an official to cut out the leopard's tongue.
translations.idiomatic: he also prayed for rain at the shrine of Ximen Bao, and when no rain came, he ordered an official to cut out the leopard's tongue.

sentences.zh: 未幾，二兒暴喪，身亦遇疾，巫以為虎、豹之祟。

translations.literal: Before long both sons died suddenly; he himself also fell ill; shamans believed it was the mischief of the tiger and leopard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both his sons died suddenly, and he himself fell ill as well. Shamans said the tiger and leopard had brought the affliction.

sentences.zh: 徵拜光祿卿，領右衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of the Imperial Domain, concurrently Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Minister of the Imperial Domain, concurrently serving as Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 與元叉同謀廢靈太后。

translations.literal: Together with Yuan Cha he plotted to depose Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yuan Cha he plotted to depose Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 遷撫軍大將軍、河南尹，仍右衞，領左右。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Henan, still Right Guard, commanding the Imperial Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Henan, retaining his post as Right Guard General and commanding the Imperial Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 與子難娶左衞將軍侯剛女，即元叉妹夫也。

translations.literal: His son Nan married the daughter of Left Guard General Hou Gang, who was Yuan Cha's brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nan married the daughter of Left Guard General Hou Gang, who was Yuan Cha's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 叉以其通姻，深相委託，三人率多俱宿禁內，時或迭出。

translations.literal: Cha because of this marital connection deeply entrusted him; the three often slept together in the inner palace, sometimes taking turns going out.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this marriage tie, Cha deeply trusted him. The three men often slept together within the inner palace, sometimes taking turns going out.

sentences.zh: 叉以康生子難為千牛備身。

translations.literal: Cha made Kangsheng's son Nan a Thousand-Ox Guard attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Cha appointed Kangsheng's son Nan to the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 康生性粗武，言氣高下，叉稍憚之，見于顏色，康生亦微懼不安。

translations.literal: Kangsheng was rough and martial by nature, his speech rising and falling in tone; Cha gradually feared him, showing it in his face, and Kangsheng too grew slightly uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng was rough and martial by nature, and his speech rose and fell without restraint. Cha gradually came to fear him, and it showed in his face; Kangsheng too grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 正光二年三月，肅宗朝靈太后于西林園，文武侍坐，酒酣迭舞。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Zhengguang, Emperor Xiaozan held court for Empress Dowager Ling at Xilin Garden; civil and military officials sat in attendance; when the wine was deep they danced in turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Zhengguang, Emperor Xiaozan held audience for Empress Dowager Ling in Xilin Garden. Civil and military officials sat in attendance, and when the wine had gone deep they danced in turn.

sentences.zh: 次至康生，康生乃為力士舞，及於折旋，每顧視太后，舉手、蹈足、瞋目、頷首為殺縛之勢。

translations.literal: When Kangsheng's turn came, he performed a warrior's dance; during the turns and twists he kept glancing at the Empress Dowager, raising hands, stamping feet, glaring, nodding—all in gestures of binding and killing.
translations.idiomatic: When Kangsheng's turn came, he performed a warrior's dance. As he spun and turned, he kept glancing at the Empress Dowager, raising his hands, stamping his feet, glaring, and nodding—all in gestures of seizing and killing.

sentences.zh: 太后解其意而不敢言。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager understood his meaning but did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager understood his intent but did not dare speak.

sentences.zh: 日暮，太后欲攜肅宗宿宣光殿。

translations.literal: At dusk the Empress Dowager wished to take Emperor Xiaozan to stay overnight at Xuanguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the Empress Dowager wished to take Emperor Xiaozan to stay the night at Xuanguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 侯剛曰：「至尊已朝訖，嬪御在南，何勞留宿？

translations.literal: Hou Gang said: "The Son of Heaven has already finished the audience; the consorts are in the south. Why trouble yourself to stay overnight?
translations.idiomatic: Hou Gang said, "The Son of Heaven has already finished his audience; the consorts are in the south quarters. Why should you trouble yourself to stay the night?

sentences.zh: 」康生曰：「至尊，陛下兒，隨陛下將東西，更復訪問誰？

translations.literal: " Kangsheng said: "The Son of Heaven is Your Majesty's son; he goes wherever Your Majesty goes—whom else need you consult?
translations.idiomatic: " Kangsheng said, "The Son of Heaven is Your Majesty's son; he goes wherever Your Majesty goes—whom else need you ask?

sentences.zh: 」羣臣莫敢應。

translations.literal: " No minister dared respond.
translations.idiomatic: " No minister dared answer.

sentences.zh: 靈太后自起援肅宗臂下堂而去。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling herself rose, supported Emperor Xiaozan's arm, and descended from the hall to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling herself rose, supported Emperor Xiaozan by the arm, and led him down from the hall.

sentences.zh: 康生大呼唱萬歲於後，近侍皆唱萬歲。

translations.literal: Kangsheng shouted "Ten thousand years!" from behind; nearby attendants all shouted "ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng shouted "Long live the Emperor!" from behind, and the attendants nearby all joined in shouting "Long live the Emperor!"

sentences.zh: 肅宗引前入閤，左右競相排，閤不得閉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozan was pulled forward into the side chamber; attendants jostled each other to block; the door could not be closed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozan was pulled forward into the inner chamber. Attendants crowded forward to block the way, and the door could not be shut.

sentences.zh: 康生奪其子難千牛刀，斫直後元思輔，乃得定。

translations.literal: Kangsheng seized his son Nan's Thousand-Ox saber, hacked Direct Attendant Yuan Sifu, and only then was order restored.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng seized his son Nan's Thousand-Ox saber and hacked down Direct Attendant Yuan Sifu; only then was order restored.

sentences.zh: 肅宗既上殿，康生時有酒勢，將出處分，遂為叉所執，鎖於門下。

translations.literal: Once Emperor Xiaozan had ascended the hall, Kangsheng, drunk, was about to go out to give orders when Cha seized him and chained him at the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xiaozan had ascended the hall, Kangsheng, still drunk, was about to go out to issue orders when Cha seized him and chained him at the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 至曉，叉不出，令侍中、黃門、僕射、尚書等十餘人就康生所訊其事，處康生斬刑，難處絞刑。

translations.literal: By dawn Cha did not emerge; he sent more than ten Palace Attendants, Yellow Gate officials, Vice Ministers, and Ministers to Kangsheng's place to interrogate the matter; Kangsheng was sentenced to decapitation, Nan to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Cha still did not emerge. He sent more than ten Palace Attendants, Yellow Gate officials, Vice Ministers, and Ministers to Kangsheng's cell to investigate the affair. Kangsheng was sentenced to decapitation and Nan to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 叉與剛並在內矯詔決之。

translations.literal: Cha and Gang, both inside, forged an edict to decide the sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Cha and Hou Gang, both inside the palace, forged an edict to confirm the sentences.

sentences.zh: 康生如奏，難恕死從流。

translations.literal: Kangsheng received sentence as reported; Nan's death was commuted to exile.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence on Kangsheng stood as reported; Nan's death sentence was commuted to exile.

sentences.zh: 難哭拜辭父，康生忻子免死，又亦慷慨，了不悲泣。

translations.literal: Nan wept and took leave of his father; Kangsheng was glad his son escaped death; Cha too was deeply stirred, yet Kangsheng did not weep at all.
translations.idiomatic: Nan wept and bade farewell to his father. Kangsheng was glad his son had been spared death. Yuan Cha too was deeply stirred, yet Kangsheng did not weep at all.

sentences.zh: 語其子云：「我不反死，汝何為哭也？

translations.literal: He told his son: "I did not rebel—why do you weep?
translations.idiomatic: He told his son, "I did not rebel—why then do you weep?

sentences.zh: 」有司驅逼，奔走赴巿。

translations.literal: " The officials drove and pressed him; he ran to the market.
translations.idiomatic: " The officials drove him on, and he ran to the execution ground.

sentences.zh: 時已昏闇，行刑人注刀數下不死，於地刻截。

translations.literal: It was already dark; the executioner struck with the blade several times without killing him; on the ground they hacked him apart.
translations.idiomatic: It was already dark. The executioner struck several times with the blade but failed to kill him, and on the ground they hacked him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 咸言禀叉意旨，過至苦痛。

translations.literal: All said he acted on Cha's orders; the excess reached extreme agony.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said he had acted on Yuan Cha's orders, and the torment went far beyond ordinary suffering.

sentences.zh: 嘗食典御奚混與康生同執刀入內，亦就巿絞刑。

translations.literal: Once Palace Provisioner Xi Hun and Kangsheng together entered with drawn blades; Hun too was executed by strangulation at the market.
translations.idiomatic: Once Palace Provisioner Xi Hun had entered the palace with Kangsheng, both with blades in hand, and Hun too was executed by strangulation at the market.

sentences.zh: 康生久為將，及臨州尹，多所殺戮。

translations.literal: Kangsheng had long been a general; when he took up provincial administration as Intendant, he killed many.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng had long served as a general, and when he took up office as provincial Intendant he put many to death.

sentences.zh: 而乃信向佛道，數捨其居宅以立寺塔。

translations.literal: Yet he believed in and turned toward Buddhism, repeatedly giving up his residences to establish temples and pagodas.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he turned to Buddhism in earnest and repeatedly gave up his own homes to build temples and pagodas.

sentences.zh: 凡歷四州，皆有建置。

translations.literal: In all, through four provinces, he had such foundations everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In all four provinces where he served, he left such foundations behind.

sentences.zh: 死時年五十四。

translations.literal: At death he was fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four when he died.

sentences.zh: 子難，年十八。

translations.literal: His son Nan was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nan was eighteen years old.

sentences.zh: 以侯剛子壻得停百日，竟徙安州。

translations.literal: Because he was Hou Gang's son-in-law, Nan's execution was stayed for one hundred days; in the end he was exiled to An Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was Hou Gang's son-in-law, Nan's death sentence was stayed for one hundred days, but in the end he was exiled to An Province.

sentences.zh: 後尚書盧同為行臺，又令殺之。

translations.literal: Later, when Minister of the Interior Lu Tong served as mobile headquarters, he again ordered Nan killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Minister of the Interior Lu Tong served as mobile headquarters, he again ordered Nan put to death.

translations.literal: Note 2: In the History of the Northern Dynasties, Biography of Xi Kangsheng, ch. 37, "又" (again) is written "叉" (Cha).
translations.idiomatic: Note 2: The Northern Dynasties version reads Yuan Cha where this text has "again," suggesting Yuan Cha ordered the killing rather than Lu Tong.

sentences.zh: 康生於南山立佛圖三層，先死忽夢崩壞。

translations.literal: Kangsheng had built a three-story Buddhist pagoda on the South Mountain; before his death he suddenly dreamed it collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng had built a three-story Buddhist pagoda on the South Mountain, and shortly before his death he dreamed suddenly that it had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 沙門有為解云：「檀越當不吉利，無人供養佛圖，故崩耳。

translations.literal: The monk Youwei interpreted it, saying: "Patron, this bodes ill; with no one to make offerings to the pagoda, it therefore collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Youwei offered an interpretation: "Patron, this is an ill omen. With no one to make offerings to the pagoda, it collapsed for that reason alone.

sentences.zh: 」康生稱然。

translations.literal: " Kangsheng agreed it was so.
translations.idiomatic: " Kangsheng agreed that this must be so.

sentences.zh: 竟及禍。

translations.literal: In the end calamity befell him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end calamity overtook him.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，贈都督冀瀛滄三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司空公、冀州刺史，又追封壽張縣開國侯，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, he was posthumously honored as Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ji, Ying, and Cang provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Minister of Works, and Governor of Ji Province; he was also posthumously enfeoffed as Founder Marquis of Shouzhang County, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, he was posthumously honored as Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ji, Ying, and Cang provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Minister of Works, and Governor of Ji Province, and was also posthumously enfeoffed as Founder Marquis of Shouzhang County with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 子剛，襲。

translations.literal: His son Gang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，青州開府主簿。

translations.literal: During Wuding he served as Chief Clerk to the Pacifying-Army headquarters of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding he served as Chief Clerk to the Pacifying-Army headquarters of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by customary rule.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his noble rank was reduced according to the usual rule.

sentences.zh: 剛弟定國，襲康生安武縣開國男。

translations.literal: Gang's younger brother Dingguo inherited Kangsheng's title as Founder Baron of Anwu County.
translations.idiomatic: Gang's younger brother Dingguo inherited Kangsheng's title as Founder Baron of Anwu County.

sentences.zh: 楊大眼，武都氐難當之孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Dayan was a grandson of the Di chieftain Yang Dang of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dayan was a grandson of Yang Dang, the Di chieftain of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 少有膽氣，跳走如飛。

translations.literal: From youth he had courage and spirit; in leaping and running he was like flight.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had courage and dash; when he leaped and ran he was swift as flight.

sentences.zh: 然側出，不為其宗親顧待，頗有飢寒之切。

translations.literal: However, as a collateral branch he was not cared for by his clan relatives and suffered keen hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: But as a collateral branch of the family he received little care from his clan kin and knew real hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 太和中，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he first entered office as Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he first entered office as Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 時高祖自代將南伐，令尚書李沖典選征官，大眼往求焉。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozu was about to march south from Dai; he ordered Minister of the Interior Li Chong to supervise selection of campaign officers, and Dayan went to request appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Gaozu was about to march south from Dai and had ordered Minister of the Interior Li Chong to supervise the selection of campaign officers; Dayan went to request a post.

sentences.zh: 沖弗許，大眼曰：「尚書不見知，聽下官出一技。

translations.literal: Chong refused; Dayan said: "Since the Minister does not recognize my worth, allow this subordinate to display one skill.
translations.idiomatic: Chong refused him. Dayan said, "Since the Minister does not recognize my worth, allow this subordinate to display one skill.

sentences.zh: 」便出長繩三丈許繫髻而走，繩直如矢，馬馳不及，見者莫不驚歎。

translations.literal: " He took out a long rope of some three zhang, tied it to his topknot, and ran; the rope stretched straight as an arrow, horses at full gallop could not catch him, and all who saw were astonished and exclaimed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: " He took out a long rope of some three zhang, tied it to his topknot, and ran. The rope stretched straight as an arrow, and horses at full gallop could not catch him. All who saw it were astonished and cried out in admiration.

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「自千載以來，未有逸材若此者也。

translations.literal: Chong said: "Since a thousand years past, there has never been such extraordinary talent as this.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "In a thousand years there has never been such extraordinary talent as this.

sentences.zh: 」遂用為軍主。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon employed as an army commander.
translations.idiomatic: " He was thereupon employed as an army commander.

sentences.zh: 大眼顧謂同僚曰：「吾之今日，所謂蛟龍得水之秋，自此一舉終不復與諸君齊列矣。

translations.literal: Dayan turned and said to his colleagues: "Today for me is what they call the season when the flood dragon finds water; from this one advance I shall never again stand on equal footing with you all.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan turned to his colleagues and said, "Today for me is what they call the season when the flood dragon finds water. From this one advance I shall never again stand on equal footing with you all.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，遷為統軍。

translations.literal: " Before long he was promoted to Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was promoted to Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 從高祖征宛、葉、穰、鄧、九江、鍾離之間，所經戰陳，莫不勇冠六軍。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Gaozu in campaigns among Wan, Ye, Rang, Deng, Jiujiang, and Zhongli, in every battle line he passed through his courage topped the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Gaozu in campaigns among Wan, Ye, Rang, Deng, Jiujiang, and Zhongli, in every battle he fought his courage topped the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，裴叔業以壽春內附，大眼與奚康生等率眾先入，以功封安成縣開國子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the court; Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and others led troops in first, and for merit he was enfeoffed as Founder Viscount of Ancheng County, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the court. Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and others led the vanguard, and for his merit Dayan was enfeoffed as Founder Viscount of Ancheng County with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除直閤將軍，尋加輔國將軍、游擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Attendant General, and soon given the additional titles General Who Assists the State and General Who Roams in Attack.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Direct Attendant General, and soon given the additional titles General Who Assists the State and General Who Roams in Attack.

sentences.zh: 出為征虜將軍、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Eastern Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Eastern Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 時蠻酋樊秀安等反，詔大眼為別將，隸都督李崇，討平之。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarian chieftains Fan Xiuan and others rebelled; an edict appointed Dayan Separate Commander under Grand Commander Li Chong to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the barbarian chieftains Fan Xiuan and others rebelled. An edict appointed Dayan Separate Commander under Grand Commander Li Chong to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 大眼妻潘氏，善騎射，自詣軍省大眼。

translations.literal: Dayan's wife, Lady Pan, was skilled at mounted archery and came in person to the army camp to join Dayan.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan's wife, Lady Pan, was skilled at mounted archery and came in person to the army camp to join her husband.

sentences.zh: 至於攻陳遊獵之際，大眼令妻潘戎裝，或齊鑣戰場，或並驅林壑。

translations.literal: When attacking formations or hunting, Dayan had Lady Pan dress in armor, sometimes riding side by side on the battlefield, sometimes driving abreast through forests and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: When attacking enemy lines or hunting, Dayan had Lady Pan dress in armor, sometimes riding side by side on the battlefield, sometimes driving abreast through forests and ravines.

sentences.zh: 及至還營，同坐幕下，對諸僚佐，言笑自得，時指之謂人曰：「此潘將軍也。」

translations.literal: When they returned to camp they sat together beneath the tent awning; before the staff officers he laughed and talked at ease, and at times would point to her and tell people: "This is General Pan."
translations.idiomatic: When they returned to camp they sat together beneath the tent awning. Before his staff officers he laughed and talked at ease, and at times would point to her and tell people, "This is General Pan."

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其前江州刺史王茂先率眾數萬次于樊雍，招誘蠻夏，規立宛州，又令其所署宛州刺史雷豹狼、軍主曹仲宗等領眾二萬偷據河南城。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his former Jiangzhou Inspector Wang Maoxian leading tens of thousands of men to encamp at Fanyong, to win over barbarians and Chinese and plan to establish Wan Province; he also had his appointed Wan Governor Lei Baolang, Army Commander Cao Zhongzong, and others lead twenty thousand men to steal and seize Henan City.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent his former Jiangzhou Inspector Wang Maoxian with tens of thousands of men to encamp at Fanyong, to win over barbarians and Chinese and plan to establish Wan Province. He also had his appointed Wan Governor Lei Baolang, Army Commander Cao Zhongzong, and others lead twenty thousand men to seize Henan City by stealth.

sentences.zh: 世宗以大眼為武衞將軍、假平南將軍、持節，都督統軍曹敬、邴虬、樊魯等諸軍討茂先等，大破之，斬衍輔國將軍王花、龍驤將軍申天化，俘馘七千有餘。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming appointed Dayan Guard General, Provisionally General Who Pacifies the South, Bearer of the Staff, commanding Army Commanders Cao Jing, Bing Qiu, Fan Lu, and other armies to attack Maoxian and the rest; he routed them, beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Wang Hua and General of Dragon Cavalry Shen Tianhua, and captured or beheaded more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming appointed Dayan Guard General, Provisionally General Who Pacifies the South, and Bearer of the Staff, commanding Army Commanders Cao Jing, Bing Qiu, Fan Lu, and other armies against Maoxian and his forces. Dayan routed them, beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Assists the State Wang Hua and General of Dragon Cavalry Shen Tianhua, and captured or beheaded more than seven thousand.

sentences.zh: 衍又遣其舅張惠紹總率眾軍，[3]竊據宿豫。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan again sent his maternal uncle Zhang Huishao to command all armies, [3] and they stealthily seized Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan again sent his maternal uncle Zhang Huishao to command all the armies, [3] and they stealthily seized Suyu.

sentences.zh: 又假大眼平東將軍為別將，與都督邢巒討破之。

translations.literal: Dayan was again provisionally made General Who Pacifies the East as Separate Commander; with Grand Commander Xing Luan he attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan was again provisionally made General Who Pacifies the East and Separate Commander, and with Grand Commander Xing Luan he attacked and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 遂乘勝長驅，與中山王英同圍鍾離。

translations.literal: He then pressed the victory in a long pursuit and, with Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying, jointly besieged Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed the victory in a long pursuit and, together with Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying, jointly besieged Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 大眼軍城東，守淮橋東西二道。

translations.literal: Dayan's army was east of the city, guarding the eastern and western routes of the Huai Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan's army was stationed east of the city, guarding the eastern and western approaches to the Huai Bridge.

sentences.zh: 屬水汎長，大眼所綰統軍劉神符、公孫祉兩軍夜中爭橋奔退，大眼不能禁，相尋而走，坐徙為營州兵。

translations.literal: As the waters rose in flood, the two armies under Army Commanders Liu Shenfu and Gongsun Zhi that Dayan commanded competed for the bridge by night and fled in retreat; Dayan could not stop them and they withdrew one after another; he was punished by exile to serve as a soldier in Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the waters rose in flood, the two armies under Army Commanders Liu Shenfu and Gongsun Zhi that Dayan commanded fought over the bridge by night and fled in retreat. Dayan could not stop them, and they withdrew one after another. He was punished by exile to serve as a soldier in Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 永平中，世宗追其前勳，起為試守中山內史。

translations.literal: During Yongping, Emperor Xiaoming, recalling his earlier merits, recalled him to serve as Acting Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongping, Emperor Xiaoming, recalling his earlier merits, recalled him to serve as Acting Administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 時高肇征蜀，世宗慮蕭衍侵軼徐揚，乃徵大眼為太尉長史、持節、假平南將軍、東征別將，隸都督元遙，遏禦淮肥。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Zhao was campaigning in Shu; Emperor Xiaoming feared Xiao Yan would raid Xu and Yang; he summoned Dayan as Chief Clerk to the Minister of War, Bearer of the Staff, Provisionally General Who Pacifies the South, Eastern Campaign Separate Commander, under Grand Commander Yuan Yao to block and defend the Huai and Fei region.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gao Zhao was campaigning in Shu, and Emperor Xiaoming feared Xiao Yan would raid Xu and Yang. He summoned Dayan as Chief Clerk to the Minister of War, Bearer of the Staff, Provisionally General Who Pacifies the South, and Eastern Campaign Separate Commander under Grand Commander Yuan Yao to block and defend the Huai and Fei region.

sentences.zh: 大眼至京師，時人思其雄勇，喜其更用，臺省閭巷，觀者如巿。

translations.literal: When Dayan reached the capital, people missed his heroic courage and rejoiced at his reappointment; in the ministries and lanes of the wards, onlookers packed the streets like a market.
translations.idiomatic: When Dayan reached the capital, people missed his heroic courage and rejoiced at his reappointment. In the ministries and lanes of the wards, onlookers packed the streets like a market.

sentences.zh: 大眼次譙南，世宗崩。

translations.literal: Dayan encamped south of Qiao; Emperor Xiaoming died.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan encamped south of Qiao, and Emperor Xiaoming died.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍遣將康絢於浮山遏淮，規浸壽春，詔加大眼光祿大夫，率諸軍鎮荊山，復其封邑。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Yan sent General Kang Xuan at Fushan to block the Huai and planned to inundate Shouchun; an edict promoted Dayan to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, had him lead all armies to garrison Jingshan, and restored his fief.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiao Yan sent General Kang Xuan to block the Huai at Fushan and planned to inundate Shouchun. An edict promoted Dayan to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, had him lead all armies to garrison Jingshan, and restored his fief.

sentences.zh: 後與蕭寶夤俱征淮堰，不能克。

translations.literal: Later, together with Xiao Baoyin, he campaigned against the Huai embankment but could not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, together with Xiao Baoyin, he campaigned against the Huai embankment but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 遂於堰上流鑿渠決水而還，加平東將軍。

translations.literal: He then cut a channel upstream of the embankment to release the water and returned; he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut a channel upstream of the embankment to release the water and withdrew. He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 大眼善騎乘，裝束雄竦，擐甲折旋，見稱當世。

translations.literal: Dayan was skilled at riding; his equipment was imposing and martial; drawing on armor and wheeling about, he was acclaimed in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan was skilled at riding, his equipment imposing and martial. Clad in armor and wheeling about, he was acclaimed in his age.

sentences.zh: 撫巡士卒，呼為兒子，及見傷痍，為之流泣。

translations.literal: He comforted and inspected the soldiers, calling them his sons, and when he saw the wounded he wept for them.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted and inspected the soldiers, calling them his sons, and when he saw the wounded he wept for them.

sentences.zh: 自為將帥，恒身先兵士，衝突堅陳，出入不疑，當其鋒者，莫不摧拉。

translations.literal: From the time he became a commander, he always placed himself ahead of the troops; charging hard formations and passing in and out without hesitation, whoever met his edge was none who failed to be shattered and brought down.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he became a commander, he always placed himself ahead of the troops. Charging hard formations and passing in and out without hesitation, whoever met his edge was shattered and brought down.

sentences.zh: 南賊前後所遣督將，軍未渡江，預皆畏懾。

translations.literal: The commanders and generals the southern rebels sent before and after, before their armies had crossed the Yangzi, were all already cowed in dread.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders and generals the southern rebels sent, one after another, were already cowed in dread before their armies had even crossed the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 傳言淮泗、荊沔之間有童兒啼者，恐之云「楊大眼至」，無不即止。

translations.literal: Legend had it that among children crying between the Huai-Si and Jing-Mian regions, those who feared them would say "Yang Dayan is coming," and none failed to stop at once.
translations.idiomatic: Legend had it that among children crying between the Huai-Si and Jing-Mian regions, those who feared them would say, "Yang Dayan is coming," and none failed to stop at once.

sentences.zh: 王肅弟子秉之初歸國也，謂大眼曰：「在南聞君之名，以為眼如車輪。

translations.literal: When Wang Su's nephew Bingzhi had just returned to the realm, he said to Dayan: "In the south I heard your name and thought your eyes were like cart wheels.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su's nephew Bingzhi had just returned to the realm, he said to Dayan, "In the south I heard your name and thought your eyes were like cart wheels.

sentences.zh: 及見，乃不異人。

translations.literal: When I met you, you were no different from other men.
translations.idiomatic: When I met you, you were no different from other men.

sentences.zh: 」大眼曰：「旗鼓相望，瞋眸奮發，足使君目不能視，何必大如車輪。

translations.literal: " Dayan said: "When standards and drums face each other and I glare and rouse myself, that is enough to keep your eyes from seeing—why must they be as large as cart wheels?
translations.idiomatic: " Dayan said, "When standards and drums face each other and I glare and rouse myself, that is enough to keep your eyes from seeing—why must they be as large as cart wheels?

sentences.zh: 」當世推其驍果，皆以為關張弗之過也。

translations.literal: " Men of the age praised his fierce valor, all thinking he did not fall short of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of the age praised his fierce valor, all thinking he did not fall short of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei.

sentences.zh: 然征淮堰之役，喜怒無常，捶撻過度，軍士頗撼焉。

translations.literal: Yet in the campaign at the Huai embankment his joy and anger were capricious; beatings exceeded measure, and the soldiers were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the campaign at the Huai embankment his joy and anger were capricious, beatings exceeded measure, and the soldiers were greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 識者以為性移所致。

translations.literal: The discerning took this to be due to a shift in character.
translations.idiomatic: The discerning took this to be due to a shift in character.

sentences.zh: 又以本將軍出為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again appointed, retaining his original rank as general, as Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed, retaining his original rank as general, as Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 常縛蒿為人，衣以青布而射之。

translations.literal: He often bound reeds into the shape of a man, clothed it in blue cloth, and shot arrows at it.
translations.idiomatic: He often bound reeds into the shape of a man, clothed it in blue cloth, and shot arrows at it.

sentences.zh: 召諸蠻渠指示之曰：「卿等若作賊，吾政如此相殺也。

translations.literal: He summoned the barbarian chieftains, pointed it out, and said: "If you make yourselves bandits, my government will kill you just like this.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the barbarian chieftains, pointed it out, and said, "If you make yourselves bandits, my government will kill you just like this.

sentences.zh: 」又北淯郡嘗有虎害，大眼搏而獲之，斬其頭懸於穰巿。

translations.literal: " Again, in Beiyu Commandery there had once been tiger attacks; Dayan grappled and captured one, cut off its head, and hung it in Rang market.
translations.idiomatic: " Again, in Beiyu Commandery there had once been tiger attacks. Dayan grappled and captured one, cut off its head, and hung it in Rang market.

sentences.zh: 自是荊蠻相謂曰：「楊公惡人，常作我蠻形以射之。

translations.literal: From then on the Jing barbarians said to one another: "Lord Yang is a wicked man—he constantly makes our barbarian form and shoots at it.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Jing barbarians said to one another, "Lord Yang is a wicked man—he constantly makes our barbarian form and shoots at it.

sentences.zh: 又深山之虎尚所不免。

translations.literal: Even mountain tigers deep in the hills did not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Even mountain tigers deep in the hills did not escape.

sentences.zh: 」遂不敢復為寇盜。

translations.literal: " They dared no longer become raiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " They dared no longer become raiding bandits.

sentences.zh: 在州二年而卒。

translations.literal: After two years in the province he died.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in the province he died.

sentences.zh: 大眼雖不學，恒遣人讀書，坐而聽之，悉皆記識。

translations.literal: Although Dayan had no schooling, he constantly had someone read books aloud; he would sit and listen and remember everything.
translations.idiomatic: Although Dayan had no schooling, he constantly had someone read books aloud. He would sit and listen and remember everything.

sentences.zh: 令作露布，皆口授之，而竟不多識字也。

translations.literal: When he ordered battle reports written, he dictated them all by mouth, yet in the end he knew few characters.
translations.idiomatic: When he ordered battle reports written, he dictated them all by mouth, yet in the end he knew few characters.

sentences.zh: 有三子，長甑生，次領軍，次征南，皆潘氏所生，氣幹咸有父風。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest Zengsheng, the second Lingjun, the third Zhengnan—all born of Lady Pan—bold in spirit and all bearing their father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: the eldest Zengsheng, the second Lingjun, the third Zhengnan—all born of Lady Pan—bold in spirit and all bearing their father's bearing.

sentences.zh: 初，大眼徙營州，潘在洛陽，頗有失行。

translations.literal: At first, when Dayan was exiled to Ying Province, Pan was in Luoyang and had rather improper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Dayan was exiled to Ying Province, Pan was in Luoyang and had rather improper conduct.

sentences.zh: 及為中山，大眼側生女夫趙延寶言之於大眼，大眼怒，幽潘而殺之。

translations.literal: When he became Administrator of Zhongshan, Dayan's daughter's husband by a concubine Zhao Yanbao spoke of it to Dayan; Dayan was enraged, imprisoned Pan, and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Administrator of Zhongshan, Dayan's daughter's husband by a concubine Zhao Yanbao spoke of it to Dayan. Dayan was enraged, imprisoned Pan, and killed her.

sentences.zh: 後娶繼室元氏。

translations.literal: Later he married his successor wife, Lady Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he married his successor wife, Lady Yuan.

sentences.zh: 大眼之死也，甑生等問印綬所在。

translations.literal: When Dayan died, Zengsheng and the others asked where the seal and sash were.
translations.idiomatic: When Dayan died, Zengsheng and the others asked where the seal and sash were.

sentences.zh: 時元始懷孕，自指其腹謂甑生等曰：「開國當我兒襲之，汝等婢子，勿有所望！

translations.literal: At the time Lady Yuan was pregnant; she pointed to her belly and said to Zengsheng and the rest: "The founding title shall be inherited by my son—you slave-girls' sons need not hope for anything!
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lady Yuan was pregnant. She pointed to her belly and said to Zengsheng and the rest, "The founding title shall be inherited by my son—you slave-girls' sons need not hope for anything!

sentences.zh: 」甑生深以為恨。

translations.literal: " Zengsheng deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: " Zengsheng deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 及大眼喪將還京，出城東七里，營車而宿。

translations.literal: When Dayan's funeral was about to return to the capital, they went seven li east of the city, pitched the funeral carts, and encamped for the night.
translations.idiomatic: When Dayan's funeral was about to return to the capital, they went seven li east of the city, pitched the funeral carts, and encamped for the night.

sentences.zh: 夜二更，甑生等開大眼棺，延寶怪而問之，征南射殺之。

translations.literal: At the second watch of the night, Zengsheng and the others opened Dayan's coffin; Yanbao, alarmed, questioned them, and Zhengnan shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch of the night, Zengsheng and the others opened Dayan's coffin. Yanbao, alarmed, questioned them, and Zhengnan shot and killed him.

sentences.zh: 元怖，走入水，征南又彎弓射之。

translations.literal: Lady Yuan was terrified, fled into the water, and Zhengnan again bent his bow and shot at her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yuan was terrified, fled into the water, and Zhengnan again bent his bow and shot at her.

sentences.zh: 甑生曰：「天下豈有害母之人。

translations.literal: Zengsheng said: "Under heaven, how could there be one who would harm his mother?
translations.idiomatic: Zengsheng said, "Under heaven, how could there be one who would harm his mother?

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He then stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then stopped them.

sentences.zh: 遂取大眼屍，令人馬上抱之，左右扶挾以叛。

translations.literal: They then took Dayan's corpse, had a man hold it mounted on horseback, and with attendants on either side supporting him they rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: They then took Dayan's corpse, had a man hold it mounted on horseback, and with attendants on either side supporting him they rebelled.

sentences.zh: 荊人畏甑生等驍勇，不敢苦追。

translations.literal: The people of Jing feared the fierce valor of Zengsheng and the others and did not dare press the pursuit hard.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jing feared the fierce valor of Zengsheng and the others and did not dare press the pursuit hard.

sentences.zh: 奔於襄陽，遂歸蕭衍。

translations.literal: They fled to Xiangyang and there submitted to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: They fled to Xiangyang and there submitted to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 崔延伯，博陵人也。

translations.literal: Cui Yanbo was a native of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanbo was a native of Boling.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，於彭城陷入江南。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou fell captive south of the Yangzi at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou fell captive south of the Yangzi at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 延伯有氣力，少以勇壯聞。

translations.literal: Yanbo had great strength; from youth he was known for courage and vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo had great strength; from youth he was known for courage and vigor.

sentences.zh: 仕蕭賾，為緣淮遊軍，帶濠口戍主。

translations.literal: He served Xiao Ze as a roving army along the Huai, concurrently garrison commander at Haokou.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xiao Ze as a roving army along the Huai, concurrently garrison commander at Haokou.

sentences.zh: 太和中入國，高祖深嘉之，常為統帥。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he entered the realm; Emperor Gaozu greatly admired him and often made him a commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he entered the realm. Emperor Gaozu greatly admired him and often made him a commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 膽氣絕人，兼有謀略，所在征討，咸立戰功。

translations.literal: His courage surpassed other men, and he combined it with strategy; wherever he campaigned and attacked, he always achieved military merit.
translations.idiomatic: His courage surpassed other men, and he combined it with strategy. Wherever he campaigned and attacked, he always achieved military merit.

sentences.zh: 積勞稍進，除征虜將軍、荊州刺史，賜爵定陵男。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service he gradually advanced; he was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Jing Province, and granted the rank of Baron of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated service he gradually advanced. He was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Jing Province, and granted the rank of Baron of Dingling.

sentences.zh: 荊州土險，蠻左為寇，每有聚結，延伯輒自討之，莫不摧殄，由是穰土帖然，無敢為患。

translations.literal: Jing Province's terrain was perilous and the barbarians of the left raided; whenever they gathered, Yanbo personally attacked them; none failed to be crushed and destroyed, and thereby the Rang region became tranquil, with none daring to cause harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province's terrain was perilous and the barbarians of the left raided. Whenever they gathered, Yanbo personally attacked them, and none failed to be crushed and destroyed. Thereby the Rang region became tranquil, with none daring to cause harm.

sentences.zh: 永平中，轉後將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: During Yongping he was transferred to Rear General and Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongping he was transferred to Rear General and Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其左遊擊將軍趙祖悅率眾偷據峽石，詔延伯為別將，與都督崔亮討之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his Left General Who Roams in Attack Zhao Zuyue leading troops to steal and seize Xiashi; an edict appointed Yanbo Separate Commander, and with Grand Commander Cui Liang he attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent his Left General Who Roams in Attack Zhao Zuyue leading troops to steal and seize Xiashi. An edict appointed Yanbo Separate Commander, and with Grand Commander Cui Liang he attacked them.

sentences.zh: 亮令延伯守下蔡。

translations.literal: Liang ordered Yanbo to defend Xia Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Liang ordered Yanbo to defend Xia Cai.

sentences.zh: 延伯與別將伊瓫生挾淮為營。

translations.literal: Yanbo and Separate Commander Yi Pisheng set camp straddling the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo and Separate Commander Yi Pisheng set camp straddling the Huai.

sentences.zh: 延伯遂取車輪，去輞，削銳其輻，兩兩接對，揉竹為絙，貫連相屬，並十餘道，橫水為橋，兩頭施大轆轤，出沒任情，不可燒斫。

translations.literal: Yanbo then took cart wheels, removed the rims, sharpened the spokes to points, paired them two by two, twisted bamboo into cables, threaded and linked them together—more than ten spans in all—laid them across the water as a bridge, and set large windlasses at both ends; they could appear and disappear at will and could not be burned or cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo then took cart wheels, removed the rims, and sharpened the spokes to points. He paired them two by two, twisted bamboo into cables, and threaded and linked them together in more than ten spans, laying them across the water as a bridge with large windlasses at both ends. The bridge could be raised or lowered at will and could not be burned or cut down.

sentences.zh: 既斷祖悅等走路，又令舟舸不通，由是衍軍不能赴救，祖悅合軍咸見俘虜。

translations.literal: Having cut off Zuyue and the others' route of escape and also blocked boats from passing, thereby Xiao Yan's army could not come to the rescue, and Zuyue's combined forces were all taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Having cut off Zuyue and the others' route of escape and also blocked boats from passing, Xiao Yan's army could not come to the rescue, and Zuyue's combined forces were all taken captive.

sentences.zh: 於軍拜平南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the army he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the field he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 延伯與楊大眼等至自淮陽，靈太后幸西林園引見延伯等。

translations.literal: Yanbo and Yang Dayan and the rest returned from Huaiyang; Empress Dowager Ling visited Xilin Garden and received Yanbo and the others in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, Yang Dayan, and the others returned from Huaiyang. Empress Dowager Ling visited Xilin Garden and received Yanbo and the others in audience.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿等志尚雄猛，皆國之名將，比平峽石，公私慶快，此乃卿等之功也。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "You all are bold and fierce in spirit—all famous generals of the realm. Recently in pacifying Xiashi, the court and the people rejoiced alike; this is your achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "You all are bold and fierce in spirit—all famous generals of the realm. In recently pacifying Xiashi, the court and the people rejoiced alike, and this is your achievement.

sentences.zh: 但淮堰仍在，宜須豫謀，故引卿等親共量算，各出一圖以為後計。

translations.literal: But the Huai embankment still remains, and plans must be made in advance. Therefore I have summoned you to measure and calculate together in person, each to submit one map for our future planning.
translations.idiomatic: But the Huai embankment still remains, and plans must be made in advance. Therefore I have summoned you to measure and calculate together in person, each to submit one map for our future planning.

sentences.zh: 」大眼對曰：「臣輒謂水陸二道，一時俱下，往無不克。

translations.literal: " Dayan replied: "Your servant maintains that the water and land routes should both advance together at once; wherever we go we shall not fail to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: " Dayan replied, "Your servant maintains that the water and land routes should both advance together at once; wherever we go we shall not fail to prevail.

sentences.zh: 」延伯曰：「臣今輒難大眼，既對聖顏，答旨宜實，水南水北各有溝瀆，陸地之計如何可前？

translations.literal: " Yanbo said: "Your servant now must take issue with Dayan. Having faced the sacred countenance, my reply should be true. South and north of the water each have trenches and ditches—how can a land plan advance?
translations.idiomatic: " Yanbo said, "Your servant now must take issue with Dayan. Having faced the sacred countenance, my reply should be true. South and north of the water each have trenches and ditches—how can a land plan advance?

sentences.zh: 愚臣短見，願聖心愍水兵之勤苦，給復一年，專習水戰，脫有不虞，召便可用，往無不獲。

translations.literal: This dull minister's short view: I hope Your Majesty's heart will pity the water troops' hardship and grant them remission for one year to train exclusively in naval warfare. If misfortune should arise, they can be summoned and deployed at once, and wherever sent they will not fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: This dull minister's short view is that Your Majesty's heart should pity the water troops' hardship and grant them remission for one year to train exclusively in naval warfare. If misfortune should arise, they can be summoned and deployed at once, and wherever sent they will not fail to succeed.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后曰：「卿之所言，深是宜要，當敕如請。」

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Ling said: "What you say is very much to the point. I shall decree as you request."
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Dowager Ling said, "What you say is very much to the point. I shall decree as you request."

sentences.zh: 二年，除安北將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year [of Zhengguang], he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 在州貪汙，聞於遠近。

translations.literal: While in the province he was corrupt; it was known far and wide.
translations.idiomatic: While in the province he was corrupt, and it was known far and wide.

sentences.zh: 還為金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Girdle.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮南將軍、行岐州刺史，假征西將軍，賜驊騮馬一匹。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as General Who Guards the South and acting Governor of Qi Province, provisionally General Who Campaigns West, and was granted one steed of the Hanxiliu breed.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Guards the South and acting Governor of Qi Province, provisionally General Who Campaigns West, and was granted one steed of the Hanxiliu breed.

sentences.zh: 正光五年秋，以往在揚州，建淮橋之勳，封當利縣開國男，食邑二百戶，尋增邑一百戶，改封新豐，進爵為子。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fifth year of Zhengguang, for his past merit at Yang Province in building the Huai bridge, he was enfeoffed as Founder Baron of Dangli County with a fief of two hundred households; soon the fief was increased by one hundred households, his enfeoffment was changed to Xinfeng, and he was advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the fifth year of Zhengguang, for his past merit at Yang Province in building the Huai bridge, he was enfeoffed as Founder Baron of Dangli County with a fief of two hundred households. Soon the fief was increased by one hundred households, his enfeoffment was changed to Xinfeng, and he was advanced in rank to Viscount.

sentences.zh: 時莫折念生兄天生下隴東寇，征西將軍元志為天生所擒，賊眾甚盛，進屯黑水。

translations.literal: At the time Mozhe Niansheng's elder brother Tiansheng came down from Long east to raid; General Who Campaigns West Yuan Zhi was captured by Tiansheng; the bandits were very strong and advanced to encamp at Heishui.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mozhe Niansheng's elder brother Tiansheng came down from Long east to raid. General Who Campaigns West Yuan Zhi was captured by Tiansheng, the bandits were very strong, and they advanced to encamp at Heishui.

sentences.zh: 詔延伯為使持節、征西將軍、西道都督，與行臺蕭寶夤討之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yanbo Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns West, and Western Route Commander, to campaign against them together with mobile headquarters chief Xiao Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yanbo Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns West, and Western Route Commander, to campaign against them together with mobile headquarters chief Xiao Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 寶夤與延伯結壘馬嵬，南北相去百餘步。

translations.literal: Baoyin and Yanbo set up camps at Maqi, north and south more than a hundred paces apart.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin and Yanbo set up camps at Maqi, north and south more than a hundred paces apart.

sentences.zh: 寶夤日集督將論討賊方略，延伯每云「賊新制勝，難與爭鋒」。

translations.literal: Baoyin daily gathered generals and commanders to discuss strategy against the bandits; Yanbo would always say, "The bandits have newly gained the upper hand; it is hard to contest their edge."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin daily gathered generals and commanders to discuss strategy against the bandits. Yanbo would always say, "The bandits have newly gained the upper hand; it is hard to contest their edge."

sentences.zh: 寶夤正色責之曰：「君荷國寵靈，總戎出討，便是安危所繫，每云賊不可討，以示怯懦，損威挫氣，乃君之罪。

translations.literal: Baoyin sternly rebuked him: "You bear the state's favor and grace, command troops on expedition—this bears on safety and peril. Always saying the bandits cannot be attacked shows cowardice, damages prestige and deflates spirit—this is your fault.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin sternly rebuked him: "You bear the state's favor and grace and command troops on expedition—this bears on safety and peril. Always saying the bandits cannot be attacked shows cowardice, damages prestige, and deflates spirit—this is your fault.

sentences.zh: 」延伯明晨詣寶夤自謝，仍云：「今當仰為明公參賊勇怯。

translations.literal: " The next morning Yanbo came to Baoyin to apologize in person, and also said: "Today I shall act on your behalf to test the bandits' courage or cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: " The next morning Yanbo came to Baoyin to apologize in person and also said, "Today I shall act on your behalf to test the bandits' courage or cowardice.

sentences.zh: 」延伯選精兵數千，下渡黑水，列陳西進以向賊營，寶夤率眾於水東尋原西北，以示後繼。

translations.literal: " Yanbo selected several thousand elite troops, crossed downstream to ford the Heishui, drew up formation and advanced west toward the bandit camp; Baoyin led forces east of the water along the plain to the northwest to show rearguard support.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanbo selected several thousand elite troops, crossed downstream to ford the Heishui, drew up formation, and advanced west toward the bandit camp. Baoyin led forces east of the water along the plain to the northwest to show rearguard support.

sentences.zh: 於時賊眾大盛，水西一里營營連接。

translations.literal: At the time the bandit forces were very strong; west of the water for a full li camps linked camp to camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the bandit forces were very strong; west of the water for a full li, camps linked camp to camp.

sentences.zh: 延伯徑至賊壘，揚威脅之，徐而還退。

translations.literal: Yanbo went straight to the bandit rampart, displayed his might and intimidated them, and slowly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo went straight to the bandit rampart, displayed his might and intimidated them, and slowly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊以延伯眾少，開營競追，眾過十倍，臨水逼蹙。

translations.literal: The bandits, thinking Yanbo had few troops, opened camp and competed in pursuit; their numbers exceeded his by more than tenfold and they pressed him hard at the water's edge.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, thinking Yanbo had few troops, opened camp and competed in pursuit. Their numbers exceeded his by more than tenfold, and they pressed him hard at the water's edge.

sentences.zh: 寶夤親觀之，懼有虧損。

translations.literal: Baoyin watched in person and feared losses.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin watched in person and feared losses.

sentences.zh: 延伯不與其戰，身自殿後，抽眾東渡，轉運如神，須臾濟盡，徐乃自渡。

translations.literal: Yanbo did not engage them; he personally brought up the rear, drew off his troops eastward across the water, and moved them as if by divinity—in an instant all were across, and only then did he cross at leisure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo did not engage them. He personally brought up the rear, drew off his troops eastward across the water, and moved them as if by divinity—in an instant all were across, and only then did he cross at leisure himself.

sentences.zh: 賊徒奪氣，相率還營。

translations.literal: The bandit troops lost their spirit and one after another returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit troops lost their spirit and one after another returned to camp.

sentences.zh: 寶夤大悅，謂官屬曰：「崔公，古之關張也。

translations.literal: Baoyin was greatly pleased and said to his staff: "Lord Cui is a Guan Yu and Zhang Fei of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was greatly pleased and said to his staff, "Lord Cui is a Guan Yu and Zhang Fei of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今年何患不制賊。

translations.literal: This year what worry is there of failing to subdue the bandits?
translations.idiomatic: This year what worry is there of failing to subdue the bandits?

sentences.zh: 」延伯馳見寶夤曰：「此賊非老奴敵，公但坐看。

translations.literal: " Yanbo galloped to see Baoyin and said: "These bandits are no match for this old servant—my lord need only sit and watch.
