translations.idiomatic: " Yanbo galloped to see Baoyin and said, "These bandits are no match for this old servant—my lord need only sit and watch.

sentences.zh: 」後日，延伯勒眾而出，寶夤為後拒。

translations.literal: " On the following day Yanbo led his troops out; Baoyin served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: " On the following day Yanbo led his troops out, and Baoyin served as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 天生悉眾來戰，延伯申令將士，身先士卒，陷其前鋒。

translations.literal: Tiansheng came with all his forces to fight; Yanbo issued strict orders to officers and men, placed himself ahead of the troops, and broke their vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng came with all his forces to fight. Yanbo issued strict orders to officers and men, placed himself ahead of the troops, and broke their vanguard.

sentences.zh: 於是勇銳競進，大破之，俘斬十餘萬，追奔及於小隴。

translations.literal: Thereupon the brave and sharp competed to advance; he routed them utterly, captured and beheaded more than one hundred thousand, and pursued the rout as far as Xiaolong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the brave and sharp competed to advance. He routed them utterly, captured and beheaded more than one hundred thousand, and pursued the rout as far as Xiaolong.

sentences.zh: 秦賊勁強，諸將所憚，朝廷初議遣將，咸云非延伯無以定之，果能克敵。

translations.literal: The Qin bandits were powerful and fierce—generals feared them; when the court first debated dispatching a commander, all said none but Yanbo could settle matters, and indeed he was able to overcome the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin bandits were powerful and fierce, and generals feared them. When the court first debated dispatching a commander, all said none but Yanbo could settle matters, and indeed he was able to overcome the enemy.

sentences.zh: 授右衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 於時万俟醜奴、宿勤明達等寇掠涇川。

translations.literal: At the time Moqi Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and others raided and plundered in Jingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Moqi Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and others raided and plundered in Jingchuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，盧祖遷、伊瓫生數將等皆以元志前行之始，同時發雍，從六陌道將取高平。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu Zuqian, Yi Pisheng, and several other commanders had all set out from Yong at the start of Yuan Zhi's advance, taking the Liuyu road to seize Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lu Zuqian, Yi Pisheng, and several other commanders had all set out from Yong at the start of Yuan Zhi's advance, taking the Liuyu road to seize Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 志敗，仍停涇部。

translations.literal: When Zhi was defeated, they still remained in the Jing region.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi was defeated, they still remained in the Jing region.

sentences.zh: 延伯既破秦賊，乃與寶夤率眾會於安定，甲卒十二萬，鐵馬八千匹，軍威甚盛。

translations.literal: After Yanbo had broken the Qin bandits, he and Baoyin led their forces to join at Anding—one hundred twenty thousand armored soldiers and eight thousand iron horses; the army's prestige was very great.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanbo had broken the Qin bandits, he and Baoyin led their forces to join at Anding—one hundred twenty thousand armored soldiers and eight thousand iron horses—and the army's prestige was very great.

sentences.zh: 醜奴置營涇州西北七十里當原城，時或輕騎暫來挑戰，大兵未交，便示奔北。

translations.literal: Chounu set camp at Dangyuan City seventy li northwest of Jing Province; at times light cavalry would briefly come to challenge, and before the main forces clashed they would show flight northward.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu set camp at Dangyuan City seventy li northwest of Jing Province. At times light cavalry would briefly come to challenge, and before the main forces clashed they would feign flight northward.

sentences.zh: 延伯矜功負勝，遂唱議先驅。

translations.literal: Yanbo, proud of his merit and confident of victory, then proposed taking the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, proud of his merit and confident of victory, then proposed taking the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 伐木別造大排，內為鎖柱，教習強兵，負而趨走，號為排城，戰士在外，輜重居中，自涇州緣原北上。

translations.literal: They felled trees to build large mantlets separately, fitted with locking pillars inside; they trained strong troops to carry them and run, calling this "barrier city"—warriors outside, baggage in the center—and from Jing Province they marched north along the plain.
translations.idiomatic: They felled trees to build large mantlets separately, fitted with locking pillars inside, and trained strong troops to carry them and run. They called this "barrier city"—warriors outside, baggage in the center—and from Jing Province they marched north along the plain.

sentences.zh: 眾軍將出討賊，未戰之間，有賊數百騎，詐持文書，云是降簿，乞且緩師。

translations.literal: As the armies were about to set out against the bandits, before battle several hundred mounted bandits, falsely holding documents and claiming they were registers of surrender, asked that the army hold its advance briefly.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies were about to set out against the bandits, before battle several hundred mounted bandits, falsely holding documents and claiming they were registers of surrender, asked that the army hold its advance briefly.

sentences.zh: 寶夤、延伯謂其事實，逡巡未閱。

translations.literal: Baoyin and Yanbo took the matter to be real and hesitated without reviewing the documents.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin and Yanbo took the matter to be real and hesitated without reviewing the documents.

sentences.zh: 俄而宿勤明達率眾自東北而至，乞降之賊從西競下，諸軍前後受敵。

translations.literal: Suddenly Suqin Mingda led troops from the northeast, while the bandits who had begged to surrender charged down from the west; the armies were attacked front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly Suqin Mingda led troops from the northeast, while the bandits who had begged to surrender charged down from the west. The armies were attacked front and rear.

sentences.zh: 延伯上馬突陳，賊勢摧挫，便爾逐北，徑造其營。

translations.literal: Yanbo mounted and charged the formation; the bandits' momentum was broken, and he at once pursued north, going straight to their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo mounted and charged the formation. The bandits' momentum was broken, and he at once pursued north, going straight to their camp.

sentences.zh: 賊本輕騎，延伯軍兼步卒，兵力疲怠，賊乃乘間得入排城。

translations.literal: The bandits were originally light cavalry; Yanbo's army included foot soldiers as well, and with strength exhausted the bandits seized the opportunity and penetrated the barrier city.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were originally light cavalry, while Yanbo's army included foot soldiers as well. With strength exhausted, the bandits seized the opportunity and penetrated the barrier city.

sentences.zh: 延伯軍遂大敗，死傷者將有二萬。

translations.literal: Yanbo's army then suffered a great defeat; killed and wounded were nearly twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo's army then suffered a great defeat; killed and wounded were nearly twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 寶夤斂軍退保涇州。

translations.literal: Baoyin gathered his troops and withdrew to hold Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin gathered his troops and withdrew to hold Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 延伯修繕器械，購募驍勇，復從涇州西進，去賊彭抗谷柵七里結營。

translations.literal: Yanbo repaired weapons and equipment, purchased and recruited fierce warriors, and again advanced west from Jing Province, setting camp seven li from the bandits' Pengkang Valley palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo repaired weapons and equipment, purchased and recruited fierce warriors, and again advanced west from Jing Province, setting camp seven li from the bandits' Pengkang Valley palisade.

sentences.zh: 延伯耻前挫辱，不報寶夤，獨出襲賊，大破之，俄頃間平其數柵。

translations.literal: Ashamed of his earlier setback, Yanbo did not report to Baoyin, went out alone to attack the bandits, and routed them thoroughly; in a brief span he leveled several of their palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of his earlier setback, Yanbo did not report to Baoyin, went out alone to attack the bandits, and routed them thoroughly. In a brief span he leveled several of their palisades.

sentences.zh: 賊皆逃遁，見兵人採掠，散亂不整，還來衝突，遂大奔敗。

translations.literal: The bandits all fled; seeing the soldiers plundering, scattered and in disarray, they returned to charge and the army suffered a great rout in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits all fled, but seeing the soldiers plundering, scattered and in disarray, they returned to charge and the army suffered a great rout in flight.

sentences.zh: 延伯中流矢，為賊所害，士卒死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Yanbo was struck by a flying arrow and was killed by the bandits; more than ten thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was struck by a flying arrow and was killed by the bandits; more than ten thousand soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 延伯善將撫，能得眾心，與康生、大眼為諸將之冠，延伯末路功名尤重。

translations.literal: Yanbo was good at commanding and comforting troops and could win men's hearts; with Kangsheng and Dayan he stood at the head of all generals, and in his final years his fame and achievement were especially great.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was good at commanding and comforting troops and could win men's hearts. With Kangsheng and Dayan he stood at the head of all generals, and in his final years his fame and achievement were especially great.

sentences.zh: 時大寇未平而延伯死，朝野歎懼焉。

translations.literal: At the time the great bandit threat was not yet pacified when Yanbo died, and court and countryside sighed and feared.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the great bandit threat was not yet pacified when Yanbo died, and court and countryside sighed and feared.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、定州剌史，諡曰武烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Rank to the Three Ministers, and Governor of Ding Province; his posthumous name was Wulie (Fiercely Bold).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Rank to the Three Ministers, and Governor of Ding Province; his posthumous name was Wulie (Fiercely Bold).

sentences.zh: 又有王足者，驍果多策略。

translations.literal: There was also Wang Zu, fierce and resourceful, skilled in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wang Zu, fierce and resourceful, skilled in strategy.

sentences.zh: 隸邢巒伐蜀，所在克捷。

translations.literal: Attached to Xing Luan's campaign in Shu, everywhere he achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Attached to Xing Luan's campaign in Shu, everywhere he achieved victory.

sentences.zh: 詔行益州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him acting Governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 遂圍涪城，蜀人大震。

translations.literal: He then besieged Fucheng; the people of Shu were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Fucheng, and the people of Shu were greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 世宗復以羊祉為益州，足聞而引退，後遂奔蕭衍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming again appointed Yang Zhi as Governor of Yi Province; Zu heard this and withdrew, and later fled to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming again appointed Yang Zhi as Governor of Yi Province. Zu heard this and withdrew, and later fled to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 次有王神念，足之流也。

translations.literal: Next there was Wang Shena—a man of Zu's kind.
translations.idiomatic: Next there was Wang Shena—a man of Zu's kind.

sentences.zh: 後自潁川太守奔江南。

translations.literal: Later he fled from his post as Administrator of Yingchuan to the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fled from his post as Administrator of Yingchuan to the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 又冀州人李叔仁，叔仁弟龍瓌，以勇壯為將統。

translations.literal: Also Li Shuren of Ji Province, and Shuren's younger brother Longgui—these, by courage and strength, were commanders of armies.
translations.idiomatic: Also Li Shuren of Ji Province and Shuren's younger brother Longgui—these, by courage and strength, were commanders of armies.

sentences.zh: 叔仁位至車騎大將軍、儀同三司、陳郡開國公。

translations.literal: Shuren reached the rank of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Rank to the Three Ministers, and Duke of Chen Commandery with founding noble status.
translations.idiomatic: Shuren reached the rank of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Rank to the Three Ministers, and Duke of Chen Commandery with founding noble status.

sentences.zh: 後為梁州刺史，歿於關西。

translations.literal: Later he served as Governor of Liang Province and died in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Governor of Liang Province and died in Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 龍瓌，正光中北征，戰死白道。

translations.literal: Longgui, in the northern campaign during Zhengguang, died in battle at Baidao.
translations.idiomatic: Longgui, in the northern campaign during Zhengguang, died in battle at Baidao.

sentences.zh: 其平州刺史王買奴、南秦州刺史曹敬、南兗州刺史樊魯、益州刺史邴虬、玄州刺史邢豹及屈祖、嚴思達、呂叵、崔襲、柴慶宗、宗正珍孫、盧祖遷、高智方，俱為將帥，並有攻討之名，而事迹不存，無以編錄。

translations.literal: Among them were Governor of Ping Province Wang Mainu, Governor of Southern Qin Province Cao Jing, Governor of Southern Yan Province Fan Lu, Governor of Yi Province Bing Qiu, Governor of Xuan Province Xing Bao, as well as Qu Zu, Yan Sida, Lü Po, Cui Xi, Chai Qingzong, Zongzheng Zhensun, Lu Zuqian, and Gao Zhifang—all were commanders and generals, all had reputations for attack and suppression, but their deeds are not preserved and cannot be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were Governor of Ping Province Wang Mainu, Governor of Southern Qin Province Cao Jing, Governor of Southern Yan Province Fan Lu, Governor of Yi Province Bing Qiu, Governor of Xuan Province Xing Bao, as well as Qu Zu, Yan Sida, Lü Po, Cui Xi, Chai Qingzong, Zongzheng Zhensun, Lu Zuqian, and Gao Zhifang—all were commanders and generals with reputations for attack and suppression, but their deeds are not preserved and cannot be recorded.

sentences.zh: 然未若康生、大眼、延伯尤著也。

translations.literal: Yet none were as prominent as Kangsheng, Dayan, and Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Yet none were as prominent as Kangsheng, Dayan, and Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：人主聞鞞鼓之響，則思將帥之臣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When a ruler hears the beat of drums, he thinks of his generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: When a ruler hears the beat of drums, he thinks of his generals and commanders.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 夷難平暴，折衝禦侮，為國之所繫也。

translations.literal: To still calamity and pacify violence, to repulse the enemy and guard against insult—on these the state depends.
translations.idiomatic: To still calamity and pacify violence, to repulse the enemy and guard against insult—on these the state depends.

sentences.zh: 康生等俱以熊虎之姿，奮征伐之氣，亦一時之驍猛，壯士之功名也。

translations.literal: Kangsheng and the others all possessed the bearing of tiger and bear, rousing the spirit of campaigning and attack; they too were the fierce warriors of their age, men whose military fame was the work of bold champions.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng and the others all possessed the bearing of tiger and bear and roused the spirit of campaigning and attack. They too were the fierce warriors of their age—men whose military fame was the work of bold champions.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 後衍復遣都督臨川王蕭宏 冊府卷三五三

translations.literal: Later Yan again sent the commander Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong — Cefu yuangui juan 353
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan again sent the commander Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong — Cefu yuangui juan 353

sentences.zh: 〈四一九二頁〉

translations.literal: "Hong" (宏) is written "Mi" (密).
translations.idiomatic: "Hong" is written as "Mi."

sentences.zh: 按蕭宏，梁書卷二二有傳，本傳及同書卷二武帝紀天監五年記載這次戰事。

translations.literal: Note: Xiao Hong has a biography in Liang shu juan 22; that biography and the Tianjian 5 entry in juan 2 of the same book (Emperor Wu's annals) record this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Xiao Hong has a biography in Liang shu juan 22; that biography and the Tianjian 5 entry in juan 2 of the same book (Emperor Wu's annals) record this campaign.

sentences.zh: 本書卷九八蕭衍傳稱之為「臨川王蕭密」，卷六五邢巒傳也有「蕭密餘軍，猶自在彼」的話。

translations.literal: This book's juan 98 biography of Xiao Yan calls him "Prince of Linchuan Xiao Mi," and juan 65 biography of Xing Luan also has the phrase "Xiao Mi's remaining army is still there."
translations.idiomatic: This book's juan 98 biography of Xiao Yan calls him "Prince of Linchuan Xiao Mi," and juan 65 biography of Xing Luan also has the phrase "Xiao Mi's remaining army is still there."

sentences.zh: 當是魏書避元宏諱改「宏」為「密」，非字訛。

translations.literal: This must be the Wei shu taboo on Empress Dowager Hu's name Hong (宏), changing "Hong" to "Mi"—not a scribal error.
translations.idiomatic: This must be the Wei shu taboo on Empress Dowager Hu's name Hong, changing "Hong" to "Mi"—not a scribal error.

sentences.zh: 他處如卷八世宗紀正始三年四月條作「蕭容」，也是諱改，九月條作「蕭宏」，乃後人所改。

translations.literal: Elsewhere, as in juan 8 Annals of Emperor Shizong, the Zhengshi 3 fourth-month entry has "Xiao Rong," also a taboo substitution; the ninth-month entry has "Xiao Hong," a later alteration by a scribe.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere, as in juan 8 Annals of Emperor Shizong, the Zhengshi 3 fourth-month entry has "Xiao Rong," also a taboo substitution; the ninth-month entry has "Xiao Hong," a later alteration by a scribe.

sentences.zh: 這裏舊本當作「蕭密」，但其人本名宏，今不回改。

translations.literal: Here the old text should read "Xiao Mi," but since the man's original name was Hong, it is not reversed here.
translations.idiomatic: Here the old text should read "Xiao Mi," but since the man's original name was Hong, it is not reversed here.

sentences.zh: 又令殺之 北史卷三七奚康生傳「又」作「叉」。

translations.literal: "Again ordered him killed" — in Beishi juan 37 biography of Xi Kangsheng, "又" (again) is written "叉" (Cha).
translations.idiomatic: "Again ordered him killed" — in Beishi juan 37 biography of Xi Kangsheng, "又" (again) is written "叉" (Cha).

sentences.zh: 按作「又」像是盧同令殺之，語意不明，疑當作「叉」。

translations.literal: Note: reading "又" (again) makes it seem that Lu Tong ordered the killing; the sense is unclear, and it is suspected the text should read "叉" (Yuan Cha).
translations.idiomatic: Note: reading "又" (again) makes it seem that Lu Tong ordered the killing; the sense is unclear, and it is suspected the text should read "叉" (Yuan Cha).

sentences.zh: 衍又遣其舅張惠紹總率眾軍 按卷九八蕭衍傳說「惠紹，衍舅子也」，不知是此脫或彼衍。

translations.literal: "Yan again sent his maternal uncle Zhang Huishao to command all armies" — note juan 98 biography of Xiao Yan says "Huishao was Yan's nephew by marriage"; it is unclear whether this is an omission here or an expansion there.
translations.idiomatic: "Yan again sent his maternal uncle Zhang Huishao to command all armies" — note juan 98 biography of Xiao Yan says "Huishao was Yan's nephew by marriage"; it is unclear whether this is an omission here or an expansion there.

sentences.zh: 然梁書卷一一張弘策傳，弘策乃蕭衍從舅，范陽方城人。

translations.literal: Yet Liang shu juan 11 biography of Zhang Hongce records that Hongce was Xiao Yan's maternal uncle by marriage, a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liang shu juan 11 biography of Zhang Hongce records that Hongce was Xiao Yan's maternal uncle by marriage, a native of Fangcheng in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 同書卷一八張惠紹傳，義陽人，不言和蕭衍有親，且不載其父名位。

translations.literal: The same book's juan 18 biography of Zhang Huishao, a native of Yiyang, does not say he was related to Xiao Yan and does not record his father's name or rank.
translations.idiomatic: The same book's juan 18 biography of Zhang Huishao, a native of Yiyang, does not say he was related to Xiao Yan and does not record his father's name or rank.

sentences.zh: 魏書以惠紹為蕭衍舅或舅子，實誤。

translations.literal: The Wei shu is mistaken in calling Huishao Xiao Yan's uncle or nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu is mistaken in calling Huishao Xiao Yan's uncle or nephew by marriage.
